# Exact primitive-ray representation at a true integer-base centroid

This is a change-of-variables lemma for mixed volume. It is not a
Grunbaum inequality or an assertion that any of its densities are
log-concave. In this note the positive fibers have full continuous
dimension d>=1. No intrinsic reduction is inferred from the formulas.

Let mu be mixed volume on the integer fibers K_z of a compact convex
body. Discard zero-volume fibers only from mu, and let P be its finite
positive-volume index set. Suppose the TRUE, unweighted centroid has
integer base j. Translate by that mixed-integer centroid, so that

    sum_z |K_z| z=0,    sum_z integral_(K_z) x dx=0.

The translated body contains the origin. Indeed a probability barycenter
of a measure supported on a compact convex set belongs to that set.
Moreover K_0 has positive d-volume: average all positive fibers with
their positive mass weights. Their Minkowski average lies in K_0 and
contains a positive-volume convex body. Thus 0 belongs to P.

Replace the body by C_*=conv union_(z in P) ({z} x K_z). This preserves
all positive integer fibers by convexity and preserves mu. It creates
no additional integer fibers: any integer base in conv(P) already has
a positive fiber by a Minkowski average of the positive source fibers,
and hence already belongs to P. Let V be the
linear span of P. The origin is in the relative interior of C_* in
V x R^d. Otherwise a nonzero supporting linear functional on that
relative space, nonnegative on C_*, would have integral zero. It would
therefore vanish on every positive fiber, contradicting the definition
of the affine span. This argument also uses that the mean-zero positive
weights put 0 in the relative interior of conv(P).

## 1. Primitive base directions and nested sections

For z!=0 write uniquely z=k p, where k is the positive gcd of the
absolute integer coordinates of z and p is primitive. Both signs of
a primitive vector are retained as different directions. Let R be the
finite collection of directions obtained from P minus {0}.

For p in R the positive fibers on its ray have indices

    p,2p,...,N_p p.

There are no gaps: if kp is positive and 1<=i<=k, convex combinations
with the origin put (i/k)K_(kp) in K_(ip), which is positive. Define

    Q_(p,k)=(1/k)K_(kp),      1<=k<=N_p.

They are nested compact convex bodies:

    Q_(p,k+1) subset Q_(p,k).

The same convex-combination argument proves this inclusion. Introduce
the bounded, compactly supported densities on R^d

    f_p(s)=sum_(k=1)^(N_p) k^d 1_(Q_(p,k))(s),
    g_p(s)=sum_(k=1)^(N_p) k^(d+1) 1_(Q_(p,k))(s).

All sums are finite. Their superlevel sets are nested convex sets, but
no concavity of a positive power of f_p or g_p is asserted.

## 2. Exact mass, centroid, and closed-cap identities

The substitution x=k s in the kp fiber has Jacobian k^d. Consequently

    M=|K_0|+sum_(p in R) integral f_p(s) ds,

    sum_(p in R) p integral g_p(s) ds=0,

    integral_(K_0) x dx + sum_(p in R) integral s g_p(s) ds=0.

These are the actual mass and the two actual centroid equations; g_p
cannot be replaced by f_p in either first-moment equation.

For EVERY closed ambient halfspace through the origin,

    H={ (z,x): a dot z+u dot x>=0 },    (a,u)!=0,

one has the exact identity

    mu(H)=|K_0 intersect {u dot x>=0}|
           +sum_(p in R) integral_(a dot p+u dot s>=0) f_p(s) ds.

Indeed the cap inequality at (kp,ks) is k(a dot p+u dot s)>=0,
with k positive. This also proves the formula for vertical halfspaces
u=0: the whole central fiber and every ray with a dot p=0 are retained.
Thus positive mass on entire boundary fibers is not dropped.

Any closed halfspace containing the centroid contains its parallel
through-centroid halfspace. The displayed identity therefore concerns
all directions relevant to the centroid's depth, not only coordinate
or fiber-parallel cuts.

## 3. The exact arithmetic radial form

Let rho be the Minkowski gauge of C_* in its relative ambient space
V x R^d. Since C_* is compact, convex, and contains 0 in its relative
interior, rho is finite and positive off 0, and

    k(p,s) in C_*  iff  k rho(p,s)<=1.

For every s for which the ray reaches at least its first integer index,
the number of included indices is exactly

    N_p(s)=floor(1/rho(p,s)).

Set it to zero when 1/rho(p,s)<1. Hence

    f_p(s)=sum_(k=1)^(N_p(s)) k^d,
    g_p(s)=sum_(k=1)^(N_p(s)) k^(d+1).

These formulas retain equality at integer radii. A gauge can be constant
at 1/k on a positive-volume set of s when C_* has an integer-base
supporting facet; those plateau fibers must be included. No null-set
argument is being used to alter the floor convention.

## 4. Specialization to one integer coordinate

There are at most two nonzero primitive directions. For positive indices
use Q_k^+=K_k/k. For negative indices it is convenient to change the
continuous sign too, using Q_k^-=-K_-k/k and coordinates (-k,-ks).
Writing f_+,g_+,f_-,g_- for these two nested density pairs gives

    integral g_+ = integral g_-,
    integral_(K_0) x + integral s(g_+-g_-)=0,

and for H={az+u dot x>=0},

    mu(H)=|K_0 intersect {u dot x>=0}|
      +integral_(a+u dot s>=0) f_+(s) ds
      +integral_(a+u dot s<=0) f_-(s) ds.

The oppositely oriented weak inequalities in the two ray contributions
are both closed, as required. Empty ray families contribute zero.

This representation exposes arithmetic power sums and nested convex
sections simultaneously. Obtaining a cap lower bound from their two
different densities and the shared convex body is an additional problem.
Neither a continuous integral replacing the integer sums nor a missing
log-concavity claim is part of this lemma.
